bull_bear.body:
- Leading market share in the Indian foundry industry, sustained despite aggressive Chinese competition in foundry and shot blasting
- Norican Group technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson product lines, plus R&D at the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru
- 'Full Foundry' offering integrating SIMPSON solutions and digital platforms such as Monetizer
- Aftermarket distribution network close to customers, described as a significant supply chain advantage in the Indian foundry sector
- Seven-year-old services performance engagement model with long-term service contracts that lock in customer productivity gains
- First-mover local manufacturing of SIMPSON technology in India, which has received strong market acceptance
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export and tariff exposure — U.S. tariffs and unresolved trade policy — The financial year began with significant disruptions from U.S. tariffs which continue to create global headwinds and affect the Company's ability to access U.S. markets; both Indian exports and the Company's own export performance saw subdued demand and export growth is expected to face near-term challenges. Direct U.S. exposure is limited but evolving trade policies may impact future expansion plans, and the Indian foundry industry derives roughly 10-15% of its business from exports.
- Geopolitical conflict and fuel-price / inflation pass-through — Conflicts in Europe and West Asia have contributed to a global slowdown and weakened business sentiment including in India; the West Asia conflict's impact on global fuel prices has introduced considerable uncertainty for FY 2026-27, with broad expectation of rising inflation that may cause cost escalation in both ongoing and new projects.
- Project deferral and extended completion timelines in capital goods — Delays, postponements and cancellations of large projects are being observed entering 2026, and management explicitly flags extended project completion timelines and liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector — a direct hit to order conversion and revenue recognition for an equipment supplier.
- Subdued demand and capacity underutilization — Management anticipates a cautious outlook for the upcoming financial year with relatively subdued demand across key industries and specifically names capacity underutilization as a challenge, which matters given the newly commissioned greenfield capacity at Tumkur.
- Intensifying competition, notably from Chinese players and new entrants — Chinese players have been aggressive in both the foundry and shot blasting segments, while large forging groups have entered the sector through acquisitions of ferrous foundries and by establishing new capacities, pressuring the Company's leading market share.
- End-market concentration in cyclical automotive and infrastructure demand — The Company's key end-use industry is automotive, supplemented by infrastructure sectors such as railways, wind energy, steel, ports and airports; demand momentum is tied to these cycles and to policy support such as the GST reduction.
- Skilled labour shortage, high attrition and long greenfield gestation — Industry challenges named by management include shortage of skilled labour and high attrition and long gestation periods for greenfield projects, which slow the automation adoption that drives the Company's equipment demand.
- Technology transition to cleaner and sustainable technologies — Adoption of cleaner and sustainable technologies is listed as a key industry challenge; progress on automation remains slow, deferring the upgrade cycle the Company sells into while requiring continued R&D and product-development investment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company designs and supplies foundry and surface-preparation equipment to the Indian foundry industry and to Norican Group customers abroad, built around its 'Full Foundry' concept that integrates DISA, Wheelabrator and SIMPSON product lines with digital platforms such as Monetizer. Alongside original equipment, it runs an aftermarket business whose services performance engagement model has completed seven years in India, using long-term service contracts and a distribution network kept close to customers. The Norican Group supports the India business through technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson lines and through R&D investment including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru.

outlook.body:
- Build capacity ahead of demand: commence and invest in the new greenfield manufacturing facility at Tumkur to serve growing domestic demand and Norican Group global requirements over the next decade
- Localise Norican technology in India — technology transfer and local manufacturing of SIMPSON products, DISA Flex machine development and new WHEELABRATOR surface-finishing solutions
- Sell the 'Full Foundry' concept — integrated foundry solutions combining DISA, Wheelabrator and SIMPSON lines with digital platforms (Monetizer / MONITIZER)
- Grow the Services / aftermarket business through long-term service contracts, greater customer proximity and lifecycle value creation, backed by a dense aftermarket distribution network
- Diversify revenue streams and explore new markets to mitigate demand risk, via geographic expansion, application-driven product development and adoption of Norican Group digital solutions
- Invest in R&D and engineering capability, including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru, for deeper global integration
- Invest in people — safe and inclusive workplace, capability development, technical and leadership training
- Run manufacturing on green power sourced from wind energy and continue CSR greening initiatives as part of the sustainability agenda
- Group-level capital deployment has been modest and confined to the wholly owned subsidiary: the Company subscribed to the equity share capital of Bhadra Castalloy Private Limited in 2015-16 and extended an interest-bearing intercompany demand loan in 2016-17 to finance the subsidiary's acquisition of a foundry; that subsidiary's operations have since been closed as no longer aligned with the core Group business. The Company had no joint venture or associate company at the end of the financial year, and there were no material changes or commitments affecting its financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the report. All related party transactions were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis under prior omnibus Audit Committee approvals, with no materially significant transactions with promoters, directors or KMP carrying potential conflict of interest, and no director holds any pecuniary relationship with the Company.
- Manufacturing plant at Tumkur already runs on wind energy, with continuing initiatives to make facilities more sustainable, infrastructure more energy efficient and to reduce energy consumption.
- CSR commitment to plant 5,000 trees over a span of five years; 2,000 trees were planted in Bengaluru in FY 2025-26, totalling 6,000 trees over the past four years.
- Certified to management system standards ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018.
- Product-level sustainability: the DISA sand plant range works towards 95% recycling of sand with efficient mixers, moulding machines are designed for energy efficiency and zero discharge to environment, and environmental control equipment (Filters) is supplied to foundries, steel and cement plants to manage dust and maintain clean air.
- Surface preparation (shot blasting and peening) machines emphasise repetitive usage of blasting media, energy saving and replacement of the age-old acid pickling process.
- A significant portion of the Company's and Norican Group's R&D is focused on helping customers reduce waste and energy consumption and increase production yield by upgrading to newer Norican technology; Norican digital / Industry 4.0 solutions monitor process efficiency, energy consumption and waste generation in real time to reduce carbon footprint and foundry scrap.
- Health and safety: in-house EHS employees to train, monitor and build awareness, health and safety management systems for reporting accidents, near misses, recordable incidents and lost time, and global audits, with a stated goal of zero incidents and elimination of all work-related injuries.
- Waste and resource efficiency: encourage recycling and waste reduction across all operations including canteen waste, reuse/recycling/donation of equipment, recycling of packaging materials and a move to digital systems to save paper.
- Education and skills: Norican Scholarship awarded to 501 students in FY 2025-26 (including 50 graduate engineering students across Karnataka, 441 for careers counselling and advancement and 10 for a Bachelor degree in Advanced Manufacturing), with approximately 4,888 students benefited to date, plus financial aid for clean water, sanitation and laboratory equipment near the manufacturing facility.
- Stated intent to actively build a more diverse workforce and leadership team, with women represented on the Board of Directors and among other Key Management Personnel.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion is a greenfield production facility built near its existing plant at Tumkur. Management states DISA India has invested in this greenfield facility to meet growing domestic demand as well as global requirements from the Norican Group; the new facility increases production capacity substantially and is expected to support the next phase of growth over the next decade. The Board's Report notes that substantial investments were made in establishing the new facility within a record timeframe during the year under review, aligned with the Company's long-term growth aspirations. Alongside the physical expansion, capability is being added through local manufacturing of SIMPSON technology in India (which has received strong market acceptance), new product introductions in the Wheelabrator range for the foundry industry, continued technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson product lines, and R&D investment including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru. No project cost, capex outlay or dated commissioning schedule is disclosed in the sections provided; management flags long gestation periods for greenfield projects and extended project completion timelines as industry-wide challenges.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Positive domestic demand outlook driven by strong automotive demand and continued infrastructure investment across railways, energy, roads, airports and shipbuilding
- GST reduction during the year welcomed across automotive, agriculture, infrastructure, railways and engineering, continuing to drive industry momentum; most automotive segments saw double-digit growth
- Indian foundry demand expected to grow steadily at 3-4% annually in the short term; India produces approximately 15 million tonnes of castings annually, second globally after China
- India's GDP growth for FY 2026-27 projected at 6.3%-6.5%, lower than previous years but still indicative of a growing economy
- Export headwinds: U.S. tariffs continue to restrict access to U.S. markets and export growth is expected to face challenges near term; the Indian foundry industry derives roughly 10-15% of its business from exports
- Rising inflation expectation may cause cost escalation in both ongoing and new projects; delays, postponements and cancellations of large projects are being observed entering 2026
- RBI policy has kept liquidity and borrowing rates stable over recent quarters, supporting economic stability
- Company outlook is cautious for the coming year — subdued demand across key industries, capacity underutilization, liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector and extended project completion timelines
- Competitive intensity rising from new entrants and large forging groups acquiring ferrous foundries, and from aggressive Chinese players in foundry and shot blasting; the Company retains leading market share
- Growth mix supported by both the OEM business (DISA Flex, SIMPSON, Wheelabrator surface finishing across foundry, railway and shipyard segments) and the Services business
- Digitization via MONITIZER gaining wider market acceptance for foundry optimisation and output from installed capacity
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: DISA India Limited, part of the global Norican Group, is a leading Indian supplier of foundry moulding and sand-plant equipment, surface-preparation machines and related aftermarket services, holding leading market share in the Indian foundry industry.

open.item: Management anticipates a cautious outlook for the upcoming financial year with relatively subdued demand across key industries, flagging capacity underutilization, liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector and extended project completion timelines.

Management expects a cautious FY2026-27 with subdued demand across key industries, capacity underutilization, liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector and extended project completion timelines.

The Board approved the re-appointment of Mr. Lokesh Saxena as Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer for a further three-year term from June 21, 2026 to June 20, 2029, subject to shareholder approval.
Shareholder approval is sought to re-appoint Mr. Lokesh Saxena as Managing Director & CEO for three years from June 21, 2026 to June 20, 2029.

To mitigate risk the Company will continue to explore new markets and diversify revenue streams through geographic expansion, application-driven product development and adoption of Norican Group digital solutions.

Continue to scale SIMPSON technology in India through local manufacturing, with Norican Group technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson product lines expected to drive further innovation.
The Company's CSR initiative to plant 2,000+ saplings annually will continue with employee participation.
The Company expects Indian foundry demand to grow steadily at 3-4% annually in the short term.

The Company had no joint venture or associate company at the end of the financial year, and there were no material changes or commitments affecting its financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the report. All related party transactions were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis under prior omnibus Audit Committee approvals, with no materially significant transactions with promoters, directors or KMP carrying potential conflict of interest, and no director holds any pecuniary relationship with the Company.|Manufacturing plant at Tumkur already runs on wind energy, with continuing initiatives to make facilities more sustainable, infrastructure more energy efficient and to reduce energy consumption.|CSR commitment to plant 5,000 trees over a span of five years; 2,000 trees were planted in Bengaluru in FY 2025-26, totalling 6,000 trees over the past four years.|Certified to management system standards ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018.|Product-level sustainability: the DISA sand plant range works towards 95% recycling of sand with efficient mixers, moulding machines are designed for energy efficiency and zero discharge to environment, and environmental control equipment (Filters) is supplied to foundries, steel and cement plants to manage dust and maintain clean air.|Surface preparation (shot blasting and peening) machines emphasise repetitive usage of blasting media, energy saving and replacement of the age-old acid pickling process.|A significant portion of the Company's and Norican Group's R&D is focused on helping customers reduce waste and energy consumption and increase production yield by upgrading to newer Norican technology; Norican digital / Industry 4.0 solutions monitor process efficiency, energy consumption and waste generation in real time to reduce carbon footprint and foundry scrap.|Health and safety: in-house EHS employees to train, monitor and build awareness, health and safety management systems for reporting accidents, near misses, recordable incidents and lost time, and global audits, with a stated goal of zero incidents and elimination of all work-related injuries.|Waste and resource efficiency: encourage recycling and waste reduction across all operations including canteen waste, reuse/recycling/donation of equipment, recycling of packaging materials and a move to digital systems to save paper.|Education and skills: Norican Scholarship awarded to 501 students in FY 2025-26 (including 50 graduate engineering students across Karnataka, 441 for careers counselling and advancement and 10 for a Bachelor degree in Advanced Manufacturing), with approximately 4,888 students benefited to date, plus financial aid for clean water, sanitation and laboratory equipment near the manufacturing facility.|Stated intent to actively build a more diverse workforce and leadership team, with women represented on the Board of Directors and among other Key Management Personnel.
currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal expansion is a greenfield production facility built near its existing plant at Tumkur. Management states DISA India has invested in this greenfield facility to meet growing domestic demand as well as global requirements from the Norican Group; the new facility increases production capacity substantially and is expected to support the next phase of growth over the next decade. The Board's Report notes that substantial investments were made in establishing the new facility within a record timeframe during the year under review, aligned with the Company's long-term growth aspirations. Alongside the physical expansion, capability is being added through local manufacturing of SIMPSON technology in India (which has received strong market acceptance), new product introductions in the Wheelabrator range for the foundry industry, continued technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson product lines, and R&D investment including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru. No project cost, capex outlay or dated commissioning schedule is disclosed in the sections provided; management flags long gestation periods for greenfield projects and extended project completion timelines as industry-wide challenges.

risks.risk: Export and tariff exposure — U.S. tariffs and unresolved trade policy
risks.note: The financial year began with significant disruptions from U.S. tariffs which continue to create global headwinds and affect the Company's ability to access U.S. markets; both Indian exports and the Company's own export performance saw subdued demand and export growth is expected to face near-term challenges. Direct U.S. exposure is limited but evolving trade policies may impact future expansion plans, and the Indian foundry industry derives roughly 10-15% of its business from exports.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and fuel-price / inflation pass-through
risks.note: Conflicts in Europe and West Asia have contributed to a global slowdown and weakened business sentiment including in India; the West Asia conflict's impact on global fuel prices has introduced considerable uncertainty for FY 2026-27, with broad expectation of rising inflation that may cause cost escalation in both ongoing and new projects.

risks.risk: Project deferral and extended completion timelines in capital goods
risks.note: Delays, postponements and cancellations of large projects are being observed entering 2026, and management explicitly flags extended project completion timelines and liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector — a direct hit to order conversion and revenue recognition for an equipment supplier.

Management anticipates a cautious outlook for the upcoming financial year with relatively subdued demand across key industries and specifically names capacity underutilization as a challenge, which matters given the newly commissioned greenfield capacity at Tumkur.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition, notably from Chinese players and new entrants
risks.note: Chinese players have been aggressive in both the foundry and shot blasting segments, while large forging groups have entered the sector through acquisitions of ferrous foundries and by establishing new capacities, pressuring the Company's leading market share.

risks.risk: End-market concentration in cyclical automotive and infrastructure demand
risks.note: The Company's key end-use industry is automotive, supplemented by infrastructure sectors such as railways, wind energy, steel, ports and airports; demand momentum is tied to these cycles and to policy support such as the GST reduction.

risks.risk: Skilled labour shortage, high attrition and long greenfield gestation
risks.note: Industry challenges named by management include shortage of skilled labour and high attrition and long gestation periods for greenfield projects, which slow the automation adoption that drives the Company's equipment demand.

risks.risk: Technology transition to cleaner and sustainable technologies
risks.note: Adoption of cleaner and sustainable technologies is listed as a key industry challenge; progress on automation remains slow, deferring the upgrade cycle the Company sells into while requiring continued R&D and product-development investment.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: DISA India Limited, part of the global Norican Group, is a leading Indian supplier of foundry moulding and sand-plant equipment, surface-preparation machines and related aftermarket services, holding leading market share in the Indian foundry industry.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs and supplies foundry and surface-preparation equipment to the Indian foundry industry and to Norican Group customers abroad, built around its 'Full Foundry' concept that integrates DISA, Wheelabrator and SIMPSON product lines with digital platforms such as Monetizer. Alongside original equipment, it runs an aftermarket business whose services performance engagement model has completed seven years in India, using long-term service contracts and a distribution network kept close to customers. The Norican Group supports the India business through technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson lines and through R&D investment including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Positive domestic demand outlook driven by strong automotive demand and continued infrastructure investment across railways, energy, roads, airports and shipbuilding
- GST reduction during the year welcomed across automotive, agriculture, infrastructure, railways and engineering, continuing to drive industry momentum; most automotive segments saw double-digit growth
- Indian foundry demand expected to grow steadily at 3-4% annually in the short term; India produces approximately 15 million tonnes of castings annually, second globally after China
- India's GDP growth for FY 2026-27 projected at 6.3%-6.5%, lower than previous years but still indicative of a growing economy
- Export headwinds: U.S. tariffs continue to restrict access to U.S. markets and export growth is expected to face challenges near term; the Indian foundry industry derives roughly 10-15% of its business from exports
- Rising inflation expectation may cause cost escalation in both ongoing and new projects; delays, postponements and cancellations of large projects are being observed entering 2026
- RBI policy has kept liquidity and borrowing rates stable over recent quarters, supporting economic stability
- Company outlook is cautious for the coming year — subdued demand across key industries, capacity underutilization, liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector and extended project completion timelines
- Competitive intensity rising from new entrants and large forging groups acquiring ferrous foundries, and from aggressive Chinese players in foundry and shot blasting; the Company retains leading market share
- Growth mix supported by both the OEM business (DISA Flex, SIMPSON, Wheelabrator surface finishing across foundry, railway and shipyard segments) and the Services business
- Digitization via MONITIZER gaining wider market acceptance for foundry optimisation and output from installed capacity

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build capacity ahead of demand: commence and invest in the new greenfield manufacturing facility at Tumkur to serve growing domestic demand and Norican Group global requirements over the next decade
- Localise Norican technology in India — technology transfer and local manufacturing of SIMPSON products, DISA Flex machine development and new WHEELABRATOR surface-finishing solutions
- Sell the 'Full Foundry' concept — integrated foundry solutions combining DISA, Wheelabrator and SIMPSON lines with digital platforms (Monetizer / MONITIZER)
- Grow the Services / aftermarket business through long-term service contracts, greater customer proximity and lifecycle value creation, backed by a dense aftermarket distribution network
- Diversify revenue streams and explore new markets to mitigate demand risk, via geographic expansion, application-driven product development and adoption of Norican Group digital solutions
- Invest in R&D and engineering capability, including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru, for deeper global integration
- Invest in people — safe and inclusive workplace, capability development, technical and leadership training
- Run manufacturing on green power sourced from wind energy and continue CSR greening initiatives as part of the sustainability agenda
- Group-level capital deployment has been modest and confined to the wholly owned subsidiary: the Company subscribed to the equity share capital of Bhadra Castalloy Private Limited in 2015-16 and extended an interest-bearing intercompany demand loan in 2016-17 to finance the subsidiary's acquisition of a foundry; that subsidiary's operations have since been closed as no longer aligned with the core Group business. The Company had no joint venture or associate company at the end of the financial year, and there were no material changes or commitments affecting its financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the report. All related party transactions were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis under prior omnibus Audit Committee approvals, with no materially significant transactions with promoters, directors or KMP carrying potential conflict of interest, and no director holds any pecuniary relationship with the Company.
- Manufacturing plant at Tumkur already runs on wind energy, with continuing initiatives to make facilities more sustainable, infrastructure more energy efficient and to reduce energy consumption.
- CSR commitment to plant 5,000 trees over a span of five years; 2,000 trees were planted in Bengaluru in FY 2025-26, totalling 6,000 trees over the past four years.
- Certified to management system standards ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018.
- Product-level sustainability: the DISA sand plant range works towards 95% recycling of sand with efficient mixers, moulding machines are designed for energy efficiency and zero discharge to environment, and environmental control equipment (Filters) is supplied to foundries, steel and cement plants to manage dust and maintain clean air.
- Surface preparation (shot blasting and peening) machines emphasise repetitive usage of blasting media, energy saving and replacement of the age-old acid pickling process.
- A significant portion of the Company's and Norican Group's R&D is focused on helping customers reduce waste and energy consumption and increase production yield by upgrading to newer Norican technology; Norican digital / Industry 4.0 solutions monitor process efficiency, energy consumption and waste generation in real time to reduce carbon footprint and foundry scrap.
- Health and safety: in-house EHS employees to train, monitor and build awareness, health and safety management systems for reporting accidents, near misses, recordable incidents and lost time, and global audits, with a stated goal of zero incidents and elimination of all work-related injuries.
- Waste and resource efficiency: encourage recycling and waste reduction across all operations including canteen waste, reuse/recycling/donation of equipment, recycling of packaging materials and a move to digital systems to save paper.
- Education and skills: Norican Scholarship awarded to 501 students in FY 2025-26 (including 50 graduate engineering students across Karnataka, 441 for careers counselling and advancement and 10 for a Bachelor degree in Advanced Manufacturing), with approximately 4,888 students benefited to date, plus financial aid for clean water, sanitation and laboratory equipment near the manufacturing facility.
- Stated intent to actively build a more diverse workforce and leadership team, with women represented on the Board of Directors and among other Key Management Personnel.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal expansion is a greenfield production facility built near its existing plant at Tumkur. Management states DISA India has invested in this greenfield facility to meet growing domestic demand as well as global requirements from the Norican Group; the new facility increases production capacity substantially and is expected to support the next phase of growth over the next decade. The Board's Report notes that substantial investments were made in establishing the new facility within a record timeframe during the year under review, aligned with the Company's long-term growth aspirations. Alongside the physical expansion, capability is being added through local manufacturing of SIMPSON technology in India (which has received strong market acceptance), new product introductions in the Wheelabrator range for the foundry industry, continued technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson product lines, and R&D investment including the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru. No project cost, capex outlay or dated commissioning schedule is disclosed in the sections provided; management flags long gestation periods for greenfield projects and extended project completion timelines as industry-wide challenges.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leading market share in the Indian foundry industry, sustained despite aggressive Chinese competition in foundry and shot blasting
- Norican Group technology transfer across the DISA, Wheelabrator and Simpson product lines, plus R&D at the Norican Competency Center in Bengaluru
- 'Full Foundry' offering integrating SIMPSON solutions and digital platforms such as Monetizer
- Aftermarket distribution network close to customers, described as a significant supply chain advantage in the Indian foundry sector
- Seven-year-old services performance engagement model with long-term service contracts that lock in customer productivity gains
- First-mover local manufacturing of SIMPSON technology in India, which has received strong market acceptance

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Export and tariff exposure — U.S. tariffs and unresolved trade policy — The financial year began with significant disruptions from U.S. tariffs which continue to create global headwinds and affect the Company's ability to access U.S. markets; both Indian exports and the Company's own export performance saw subdued demand and export growth is expected to face near-term challenges. Direct U.S. exposure is limited but evolving trade policies may impact future expansion plans, and the Indian foundry industry derives roughly 10-15% of its business from exports.
- Geopolitical conflict and fuel-price / inflation pass-through — Conflicts in Europe and West Asia have contributed to a global slowdown and weakened business sentiment including in India; the West Asia conflict's impact on global fuel prices has introduced considerable uncertainty for FY 2026-27, with broad expectation of rising inflation that may cause cost escalation in both ongoing and new projects.
- Project deferral and extended completion timelines in capital goods — Delays, postponements and cancellations of large projects are being observed entering 2026, and management explicitly flags extended project completion timelines and liquidity constraints in the capital goods sector — a direct hit to order conversion and revenue recognition for an equipment supplier.
- Subdued demand and capacity underutilization — Management anticipates a cautious outlook for the upcoming financial year with relatively subdued demand across key industries and specifically names capacity underutilization as a challenge, which matters given the newly commissioned greenfield capacity at Tumkur.
- Intensifying competition, notably from Chinese players and new entrants — Chinese players have been aggressive in both the foundry and shot blasting segments, while large forging groups have entered the sector through acquisitions of ferrous foundries and by establishing new capacities, pressuring the Company's leading market share.
- End-market concentration in cyclical automotive and infrastructure demand — The Company's key end-use industry is automotive, supplemented by infrastructure sectors such as railways, wind energy, steel, ports and airports; demand momentum is tied to these cycles and to policy support such as the GST reduction.
- Skilled labour shortage, high attrition and long greenfield gestation — Industry challenges named by management include shortage of skilled labour and high attrition and long gestation periods for greenfield projects, which slow the automation adoption that drives the Company's equipment demand.
- Technology transition to cleaner and sustainable technologies — Adoption of cleaner and sustainable technologies is listed as a key industry challenge; progress on automation remains slow, deferring the upgrade cycle the Company sells into while requiring continued R&D and product-development investment.

JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.

hero.oneLiner: DISA India Limited, part of the global Norican Group, is a leading Indian supplier of foundry moulding and sand-plant equipment, surface-preparation machines and related aftermarket services, holding leading market share in the Indian foundry industry.
